q: Will I lose my low first-mortgage rate?
a: It depends on the option. A HELOC or home equity loan is a second loan, so your first mortgage stays in place. A cash-out refinance replaces your first mortgage with a new one, with a new rate, term and payment. Pat's own refinance guide notes that if you already have a low rate, refinancing the first mortgage may not be ideal, and a HELOC or home equity loan can be an alternative. Pat will compare the options for your numbers.

q: Can rental income from an ADU count toward qualifying?

q: What factors affect my mortgage interest rate?
a: Your credit profile, loan type, property type, occupancy, down payment or equity, loan term, points and current market conditions can all affect pricing. The lowest advertised rate is not always the lowest total-cost option.

q: What is the difference between pre-qualification and pre-approval?
a: Pre-qualification is usually an early estimate based on information you provide. A pre-approval involves a deeper review of your credit, income, assets and debts. Because the information is verified, a pre-approval generally carries more weight with real estate agents and sellers.
